top_story: Iran’s leadership has turned the 3–4 July funeral rites for Ali Khamenei in Tehran into a mass display of regime continuity after his killing at the outset of the war with the US and Israel, with senior officials and allied networks using the ceremonies to project cohesion under pressure. The scale and duration of the six-day mourning period signal an effort to convert grief into political legitimacy at a moment of acute uncertainty inside Iran and across its regional alliances. That show of organized state strength contrasts sharply with Gaza, where Israel’s 25 June strike on tents sheltering displaced Palestinians on the beach underscored how the war’s civilian burden continues to fall most heavily on already besieged communities. The regional picture is one in which governments are mobilizing symbolism and force in parallel, while ordinary people absorb the deepest human cost.
